reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the pair, reread Annexes 1, 2 and 7 and independently recalculated the credit allocations and profiling level conditions. Rechecked the graduation project and exemption conditions against the underlying regulations. Reconsidered the three legal plans against their current workbook evidence and checked that the six alignments express substantive overlaps without presenting course equivalence or professional qualification. This was a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The Dutch-taught 180 EC LLB comprises a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling. The common 67.5 EC major includes the eight first-year courses and one 7.5 EC graduation project. The least specialized multidisciplinary route requires general jurisprudence and eight of ten legal choices. The first eight include three advanced choices, one of which is a Private Law in Perspective option illustrated by Employment Law. The first listed capstone is International and European Law. The example leaves the 45 EC of non-law electives open within the prescribed level constraints. The broader official Notarial and Toga routes have different requirements. The illustrated multidisciplinary route requires the other two law choices beyond 180 EC for the professional civiel effect pathway.

Annex 1 requires at least 45 EC at level 3. This selection contributes 37.5 advanced EC in the major, so 7.5 EC must be taken at level 3 in profiling plus another 7.5 EC at level 2 or 3. Annex 2 requires 120 earned EC including all first-year courses before the graduation project. The student course program starts with the common legal foundations before more specialized and procedural work. Art. 4.2 leaves course-specific conditions to the course catalog. Annex 7.2.2 describes exemptions on request for eligible UCR graduates who have completed 45 EC of legal courses. It cites older course codes and a specific subject condition for the Senior Project. The comparison does not assume that the current codes or the unscheduled optional research satisfy these provisions.

The broad plan uses all seven Law, Society and Justice courses, connecting comparative legal foundations, human rights, private law, criminal law, public and constitutional institutions, international law and EU law to empirical and normative inquiry. The public plan concentrates institutions, EU politics, conflict, international governance, collective action and historical research. History of warfare and empire place conflict and state power in context rather than carrying doctrinal weight. The business plan uses comparative private law, international contracts and trade, finance and accounting, digital strategy, AI in business and market research to examine how commercial relationships are governed. It supports the technology interest but lacks a dedicated Dutch employment or notarial curriculum. The six substantive rows cover concrete shared content. Ethics supports jurisprudence and comparative constitutional law supports analysis of Dutch public institutions, while procedure, advanced domestic doctrine, employment and notarial work and independent legal research remain distinct. UCR’s historical and empirical methods support research literacy in the selected plans without substituting for a law capstone.
